rationale.conceptual: Numerical solution of dislocation pile-up equations involves non-trivial force-balance systems and root-finding for stress under critical spacing or force, requiring careful implementation of the paper's derived equations and yield criteria. It goes beyond plug-and-play library calls.
rationale.execution: The pipeline is a simple sequence: validate solvers, produce two CSV files. Only standard Python libraries (NumPy/SciPy) are needed, and I/O is minimal. No complex orchestration or external data fetching.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires numerically solving discrete dislocation equilibrium equations for two cases, applying yield criteria, and fitting Hall-Petch slopes. The underlying physics is non-trivial but well documented in the paper; implementation involves root-finding for small systems. The pipeline is straightforward (a few CSV outputs). No GPU, tiny data.

compute_estimate.reasoning: Solving discrete equations for fewer than 50 dislocations is CPU-only; memory footprint is negligible and no external datasets are used.
